newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Shares in KLM rise despite poor results.
newsitem.headline: Shares in KLM rise despite poor results.

text.p: Shares in Dutch airline KLM rose on the Amsterdam stock exchange on Wednesday despite a plunge in 1996/97 net profits to 236 million guilders from 547 million in the previous year.
"The reason for the price reaction is the resignation of (CEO) Pieter Bouw," a dealer said. "Bouw really struggled with (KLM partner) Northwest's management."
At 0915 GMT, KLM shares were up 1.90 guilders at 60.10 guilders after trading up to 60.70 -- a new year-high.
KLM said on Wednesday Bouw planned to resign on August 5 and would be replaced by Chief Operating Officer Leo van Wijk.
"I think it is very positive that Van Wijk is taking over as everyone regards him as quite a strategist," said Bert van Hoogenhuyze, airlines analyst at brokers Amstgeld.
